prompt:
In the video game Asteroid Blaster, there are a total of five rounds on the first level. During each round, asteroids appear on the screen and a player must blast as many asteroids as possible before time expires. This becomes more difficult because the number of asteroids increases with each round. The table shows the number of asteroids for each of the first three rounds.

| Round | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Asteroids | 1 | 8 | 27 | | |

If this pattern continues, how many asteroids will there be to destroy in Round 4?

solutions.title: Differences
solutions.body:
The differences are 7 and 19. For cubes the differences themselves grow by 12, 18, 24, … (6 more each time), so the next difference is $19 + 18 = 37$ and Round 4 has $27 + 37 = 64$.

**Answer: 64**

prompt:
In the video game Asteroid Blaster, there are five rounds on the first level. The amount of time within which a player must blast all the asteroids increases each round. The table shows the time limit, in seconds, for each round.

| Round | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seconds | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | |

If this pattern continues, what is the maximum number of seconds allotted to complete all five rounds of this level?

solutions.title: Doubling
solutions.body:
Each time limit doubles, so Round 5 gets 32 seconds. Total: $2 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 32 = 62$ seconds.

**Answer: 62 seconds**

prompt:
In the video game Asteroid Blaster, the first level has five rounds. The number of asteroids in Rounds 1, 2 and 3 is 1, 8 and 27, and this pattern continues for Rounds 4 and 5. The number of points awarded for blasting each asteroid also increases with each round, as shown in the table.

| Round | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Points (per asteroid) | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 |

How many points will a player earn for blasting all the asteroids in Rounds 1 through 4 and blasting $\frac25$ of the asteroids in Round 5 before time expires?

solutions.title: Pattern $10n^4$
solutions.body:
In round $n$ there are $n^3$ asteroids worth $10n$ points each, so a full round is worth $10n^4$: $10(1 + 16 + 81 + 256) = 3540$ for rounds 1–4, plus $\frac25 \cdot 10 \cdot 625 = 2500$: total 6040.

**Answer: 6040 points**
